Video Converter: Convert to MP4 or WebM Locally

Choose a video and the MP4 or WebM format your destination accepts, then convert locally and download the result. Check picture and sound in the destination app. This tool changes format; it does not promise a smaller file.

Convert a local video file

Use one video track and at most one audio track. Unsupported tracks stop conversion rather than disappearing silently.

Choose a video to start.Download video

Processing stays on your device. Wait for a download link, save the new file and test it in the app that rejected the original. Your source is unchanged. An unsupported browser codec can prevent a particular conversion.

Choose the format your destination accepts

MP4 with H.264 and AAC is a useful starting point when a sharing or editing app asks for MP4. The container and the codecs inside it both matter: renaming a MOV or WebM extension does not perform conversion.

WebM with VP9 and Opus is an option when a website or app accepts that combination. Check the destination's requirements first. A playable result in this browser does not prove every target app can read it.

The converter copies compatible encoded streams where possible and re-encodes other codecs when the browser supports the target. Re-encoding can change visual or audio quality, and output size can increase. Use the video compressor when your main goal is a smaller file with explicit bitrate and resolution controls.

Check the saved result

  1. Download after conversion finishes. A full progress bar alone is not a saved file.
  2. Play through important sections and the end. Check sound, framing, orientation and any visible text.
  3. Open or upload it in the intended destination. Its own duration, size or codec rules can still reject a valid file.

Keep the original for archival or professional editing. Captions, extra audio tracks, HDR appearance and metadata are not guaranteed to survive conversion. The tool rejects multiple video or audio tracks; use a desktop editor for those projects.

Try an original sample before choosing private footage

Download the four-second H.264/AAC MOV to test MP4 output. Download the four-second VP9/Opus WebM to test a change of codecs. Both are synthetic test patterns with a steady tone.

All three downloaded outputs fully decoded. In the MOV-to-MP4 sample, decoded picture and audio checksums matched the source. This identity result is specific to that compatible-stream sample. Transcoding and codec padding can change reported duration; check timing in the destination.

If a conversion cannot finish

Try the other output format when a browser cannot encode the selected codecs. For a damaged, encrypted, unusually large or multi-track source, use a desktop converter that supports that file. A new extension cannot repair missing frames or an absent soundtrack.

The input limit is 250 MB, and device memory can impose a smaller practical limit. Cancel stops an active conversion without creating a partial result. If a file is already compatible, another conversion may be unnecessary.

Continue your media task

Save one frame as PNG. Need only the soundtrack? Extract M4A or WAV. Need a short looping image without audio? Convert a segment to GIF. These are different output tasks, so check the destination before choosing one.

Processing and test scope

Conversion uses self-hosted Mediabunny. MPL-2.0 license · Original source package. No video content is sent to a conversion server.

Browser decoding and encoding support varies. The shared samples show a bounded test, not every possible MOV, WebM or MP4 variant. The tool adds no watermark and does not promise quality improvement or smaller output.
